standards_review.notes: All seven subjects in 6ef1fcd7ff61de502255df4e4ef1fad7320f3d0e..HEAD use an allowed fix/feat type and analytics scope, imperative wording, and subjects below the documented 100-character limit.

Exported functions retain explicit return types and ES-module extensions, but the new trace module uses a prohibited deep relative import, its ownership-index function exceeds the documented function size, and the modified cost-enricher crosses the documented file-size limit. Evidence is limited to the 25 Git-tracked changed paths; the untracked run directory was excluded.

The default .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md is absent; AGENTS.md identifies the existing canonical .ai-run/guides/security/security-practices.md, which was read instead. No concrete new security issue was found: raw transcript captures use an internal symbol, dispatch exports allowlist fields, and new timeline labels use escaping or text nodes. No outbound attribution-header changes or hardcoded credentials were identified.

finding_status.notes: claude-trace.ts:1 now imports ParsedSession through the required @/ alias; the extracted Claude helpers use the same alias.
claude-trace.ts:122-131 now orchestrates separate ownership, transcript-claim, acknowledgement, cycle and relationship helpers. Each extracted function is within the documented size limit.

claude-ownership.ts:41-119 collects family-wide response/tool claims and resolves canonical owners through evidenced ancestry before claude-trace.ts builds relationships. Unsupported ownership stays unresolved instead of selecting the first transcript.

claude-trace.ts:44-52 gathers all transcript claimants and marks a multiply claimed tool conflicting before relationship construction. All claimants are excluded from resolved children, and claude-dispatch-allocation.ts:87-103 prevents exact allocation.
claude-lifecycle.ts:17-50 reads only supported protocol envelopes, gathers notifications from every owner transcript, and deduplicates by exact identities before matching nested dispatches.

claude-trace.ts:55-89 compares acknowledgement identities against tool metadata and marks both contradictory tool mappings conflicting. claude-lifecycle.ts:85-101 selects by unique tool claim, and conflicted dispatches cannot receive exact allocation.

dispatch-extractor.ts:55-68 preserves acknowledgement agentId and taskId. claude-lifecycle.ts:71-82 matches those identities without requiring a child transcript and rejects conflicting tool/task evidence.
cost-enricher.ts is now 398 content lines and imports the cohesive Claude allocation implementation from claude-dispatch-allocation.ts; shared pricing/window helpers live in dispatch-allocation.ts.

dispatch-extractor.ts:71-144 reports incomplete extraction for recognized tools without identity or valid timing and commands without valid timing. cost-enricher.ts:371-374 forwards completeness; payload-builder.ts:115-117 retains aggregate fallbacks when false.

claude-ownership.ts resolves stable native message UUID ownership across the family. dispatch-extractor.ts:99-120 emits each command UUID/ordinal once under its canonical owner while preserving distinct invocations.

dispatch-extractor.ts:55-68 preserves explicit block and acknowledgement is_error/isError/failed status. claude-lifecycle.ts:91-101 retains failed synchronous terminal timing; payload-builder.ts:58-59 counts it as a failure.

usage-readers.ts:157-190 obtains keyed response ownership from buildClaudeOwnership before deduplication, separately from fuller usage selection. Ambiguous owners remain unallocated, and claude-dispatch-allocation.ts:18-24,98-109 prevents uncertain own/inclusive values being labeled exact.
